title: Perseus Biotech VPC sprint proposal + terraform module notes
body:
Purpose / context:
This is an internal working proposal for a phased VPC + on-prem edge deployment for Perseus Biotech (short: Perseus). They plan to host PHI-adjacent model endpoints inside their VPC with private subnets and a customer-managed bastion for maintenance. This doc captures a sprint-based rollout, terraform module usage notes, sizing assumptions (CPU/GPU/IO), expected performance targets, a rollback plan, and a Q&A list for the next customer sync.

Executive summary (short):
- Goal: deliver a Private deployment (VPC-first, optionally hybrid on-prem) supporting 30 qps peak for classification/NER endpoints and 8 concurrent generation sessions for the longest usecases.
- Target SLOs: p95 latency <= 120ms for classification, p95 token latency <= 200ms for 512-token generation (batching enabled).
- Phased approach: 3 two-week sprints (preflight, pilot, scale), then handoff to Perseus infra team.
- Primary risks: customer network egress limits, KMS/HSM key policies, GPU driver mismatch for quantized runtimes.

Sprint plan (high level):
- Sprint 0 (preflight, 2w): infra discovery, network baseline tests, minimal TF plan that brings up control-plane connector + test GPU node in staging. Deliverable: preflight checklist and terraform plan that succeeds in Perseus dev VPC.
- Sprint 1 (pilot, 2w): deploy 1 serving cell (2x A10G equiv) behind internal ALB, enable KV prefix caching, validate runtime images, run synthetic load tests. Deliverable: pilot runbook + perf dashboard links.
- Sprint 2 (scale+hardening, 2w): add autoscaling policy, integrate KMS for keys, enable TLS mutual auth for control plane, run soak tests. Deliverable: production-ready TF modules and cutover checklist.

Capacity / sizing assumptions (working numbers):
- Expected workload: bursty inference for drug screening UIs (spikes ~30 qps), background batch embedding jobs overnight (100k embeddings/day).
- Model profiles:
  - Small classifier (7B fp16) for NER: ~20ms per request on A10G-equivalent with batching 8.
  - Generation (13B quantized int8): ~180ms p95 for 512 tokens, memory-limited if KV cache stored on GPU (per-session KV ~2.5GB).
- Baseline node sizing recommendation:
  - Serving node type: 2x A10G-equivalent GPUs per node (allows local redundancy), 96GB host RAM, 2x 1.6TB NVMe for model shards/KV persist cache.
  - Control plane/sidecars: 4 vCPU, 16GB RAM, EBS 200GB encrypted.
- Cluster sizing for target qps: start with 3 serving nodes (6 GPUs) to meet 30 qps with headroom for autoscaling; expect steady-state cost/perf tradeoffs when scaling to 5 nodes for larger throughput.

Networking & security notes:
- Private subnets only. Control plane uses a customer-managed NAT for outbound CRLs and container registries. Confirm egress bandwidth limits (Perseus currently has 250Mbps egress in the dev VPC—may need bump to 1Gbps for model pulls).
- KMS: customer prefers Cloud KMS with HSM-backed keys. TF modules include optional kms_key_id var; ensure IAM role mapping is explicit.
- Audit logs: forward container and inference logs to customer SIEM via a secure syslog endpoint. Add a log-rotation policy to avoid disk saturation.

Terraform module notes (practical):
- Use redwood/private-deploy/v1 module as baseline; create an overlay module perseus/custom that sets naming and tagging conventions.
- Key variables we patch in overlay:
  - public_subnet_ids: [] (none)
  - private_subnet_ids: [list provided by customer]
  - gpu_profile: "a10g-2x" (string var that maps to cloud flavor)
  - kms_key_id: ""
- Example snippet (pseudo-TF, intentionally simplified):

module "perseus_private" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-modules.git//modules/private-deploy?ref=v1.3.0"

  project         = "perseus-rd"
  env             = "prod"
  private_subnets = var.private_subnets
  management_cidr = var.management_cidr
  gpu_profile     = "a10g-2x"
  kms_key_id      = var.kms_key_id

  tags = merge(var.common_tags, { customer = "perseus" })
}

Implementation notes for TF: keep state short-lived in a remote backend (s3/gs) with state locking. We recommend splitting modules: network (VPC/subnets), infra (compute, disks), redwood-control (agents/sidecars), and ops (monitoring, logs). Keep module outputs minimal and use remote state data sources where needed.

Storage & KV caching:
- KV cache heuristic: allocate 3GB GPU-side KV per concurrent long-running session. With 8 concurrent generation sessions, reserve ~24GB of GPU memory for KV cache across the cluster. That maps to at least 2x A10G nodes if model KV cache stored on device.
- Persistent NVMe used for model artifact staging and swap for cold sessions. Use a mount path /var/lib/redwood/models and ensure inode counts are sufficient for many small shard files.

Driver/runtime ops:
- We need GPU driver and CUDA compatibility checklist. Customer's on-prem infra currently reports CUDA 11.2; runtime requires CUDA 11.8+ for optimized kernels. Options: bump drivers (preferred) or use a fallback runtime image with less-optimized kernels. Documented in the ops-runbook.
- Quantization note: when using int8 quantized variants we observed subtle quality regressions for some Perseus prompts in internal evals. Add a quality-monitoring eval in the pilot focusing on recall for high-value terms (drug names).

Monitoring & rollback:
- Baseline dashboards: per-node GPU utilization, per-model p95 latency, request errors, token count, and cache hit ratio.
- Rollback plan (fast):
  - If pilot has >5% request error increase or p95 latency >2x target for 30 minutes, programmatically scale down new nodes and route traffic to previous serving variant (hosted or alternate model with fewer params).
  - Maintain a fallback small hosted endpoint managed by Redwood that can be activated via routing policy.

Open questions / items for next customer meeting (to confirm):
- Confirm egress bandwidth SLAs on production VPC and expected maintenance windows for kernel/driver upgrades.
- Confirm acceptance criteria for quality regression (we propose A/B tests against the production prompt set with 95% recall threshold for named entities).
- Does Perseus require FIPS-enabled crypto for KMS/transport? If yes, some runtime images must be rebuilt.
- Who owns day-2 ops (Perseus infra team or Redwood SRE support contract)? We need a contact for emergency escalations.

Short checklist for preflight (actionable):
- [ ] Customer provides private_subnet_ids and VPC CIDR mapping.
- [ ] Shared bastion IP allowlist for control-plane maintenance.
- [ ] Confirm KMS key ARN and IAM role for Redwood service account.
- [ ] Run a 30-minute synthetic load (locust) to validate p95 targets against pilot config.
- [ ] Driver compatibility test (run nvcc --version on one GPU host).

Unresolved implementation notes / TODOs (internal):
- Add terraform fmt/lint CI to the overlay repo and a gating PR that verifies plan against a mock backend.
- Add a short script to convert Perseus VM SKU names to our internal gpu_profile mapping.
- Create a short runbook snippet for on-call to rotate KMS keys in an emergency without downtime (key rotation pattern).

Appendix: quick cost sketch (monthly, rough):
- 3 nodes (6x A10G-equivalent): compute ~ $18k/mo, NVMe storage + EBS ~ $1.2k/mo, network egress variable. Ops and support add-on TBD (enterprise SLA).

Contact / next steps:
- Owner: Maya Chen (redwood-inference)
- Schedule: request Perseus infra availability window for Sprint 0 between Oct 7–18.
- Next sync items: confirm KMS details, VPC egress envelope, and pilot test dataset access procedure.

Notes-to-self (rough):
- Keep pilot image tags immutable (image: redwood/private-serving:2024-09-perseus).
- Remind solutions engineering to run the prompt set through eval harness before enabling int8 for the generation model.
